thread.title: Did an Emotional Elon Musk Save Tesla's Stock at the Annual Meeting?

author: Home
title: Did an Emotional Elon Musk Save Tesla's Stock at the Annual Meeting?
text:
Elon Tried Hard: He was emotional. He paused for what seemed like 10 minutes to think about a question before answering. He said Tesla ( TSLA ) makes its cars with love unlike the bean counters at Ford ( F ) and General Motors ( GM ) . He said the night before be drove an almost fully autonomous Tesla around California at night. He again reiterated Tesla doesn't need a capital raise . He even admitted to often making wildly optimistic projections that won't get met. In short, Elon Musk did everything he could -- in true quirky Musk form -- to stem the decline in the stock and quiet the bears at the company's annual meeting Tuesday evening. While the market is responding well to the presentation (shares were rising 1.5% in premarket trading), the reality is that Tesla has to release numbers to back up Musk's latest claims. It has to issue a press release updating second-quarter trends, something to signal to the market that yes, Tesla doesn't need to raise capital by year-end. If not, then Tesla's stock is likely to resume its slide as investors price in a crushing capital raise and more quarters of production hell. On another note, there's good news for Harley-Davidson ( HOG ) -- Musk said Tesla won't be making electric motorcycles .
Watch This Market: If the markets have lulled you to sleep this week, now would be a great time to wake the hell up. Risk is back on the rise, and stocks could make a violent turn. Italian bonds dropped for the second day on Wednesday on fears the European Central Bank will start unwinding its quantitative easing program at its June 14 meeting. Couple that with a still precarious political situation in Italy, the factors that sent stocks reeling early last week are coming back to the forefront. Meanwhile, it's on the unnerving side of things to see stocks under pressure Wednesday despite China's willingness to buy $70 billion more in goods from the U.S. Isn't that supposed to be a positive development? It's as if the market is looking past this knowing China's gesture is unlikely to impress President Trump. Hence, the G-7 later this week could bring a series of Trumpian verbal bombs that rattle investor confidence. Also mildly worrying: Shares of global economic bellwether Caterpillar ( CAT ) have fallen 1% over the past five days vs. a 1% gain for the Dow Jones Industrial Average . Other big-name industrials such as UPS ( UPS ) and FedEx ( FDX ) have also underperformed the Dow of late.
